correctness.rationale: For N=3^k, write W=μ^k(1). It is palindromic with endpoint ones, and distinct W blocks in C=μ^k(C) have at least one whole zero block between them because C has no consecutive ones. A length-N window therefore has ones from at most one W and is either all zero or a zero-padded prefix or suffix of W (including the whole W). Every needed representative is realized inside μ^k(010)=0^N W 0^N, since 010 occurs. At positive weight j the zero-padded prefixes all yield the same necklace and the suffixes give its reversal. With zero-based positions p_i of the ones, the internal gap p_(i+1)−p_i is 2·3^r−2(1+3+⋯+3^(r−1))=3^r+1 with r=v_2(i), by the binary-to-ternary digit carry. Every internal gap is even, while the circular closing gap N−p_j is positive and odd. Thus a rotation identifying a necklace with its reversal must align that unique closing gap, equivalently reverse the internal gap list onto itself. For j=2^a the valuation list is symmetric under i↦j−i. Otherwise, for j>1, the unique largest internal gap occurs at i equal to the largest power of two at most j−1. A palindrome would put that gap at i=j/2, forcing j to be a power of two. The empty internal list at j=1 is symmetric, including k=0. This gives one all-zero class, two candidates at each positive weight and exactly k+1 identifications, for 2^(k+1)−k.
residual_risks: The recorded Python checks are finite; the argument above, not their pass marker, establishes all k.
A class is counted when some representative occurs, not only when all rotations occur.

evidence: Abelian complexity at 3^k is 2^k+1; the general bounds put cyclic complexity between abelian and ordinary factor complexity. The Cantor Lie-complexity formula applies to all lengths, but to full rotation orbits only.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader coverage in length does not imply the count when the criterion or equivalence is different. The abelian lower bound allows both one and two necklaces at a weight, the question settled here.

evidence: The abelian recurrence specifies which weights occur, not whether the reverse necklace is a second class. A scattered-01 count is not invariant under cyclic rotation (already 01 and 10 differ). Ordinary factor counts, even if known exactly, do not give the rotation identifications.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The additional marked circular gap and maximum-gap symmetry argument are not parameter substitutions in those results. The unconfirmed precise attribution of the ordinary factor formula is not needed by the proof or the originality distinction.

evidence: Cassaigne et al. define exactly the equivalence used here, but the inspected treatment has no located Cantor-specific triadic profile. Bell–Shallit §2 explicitly requires all rotations for Lie complexity and contrasts this with the some-rotation criterion.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Conjugacy and binary necklaces match; Lie, factor, permutation, abelian, and finite-word circular BWT run complexities do not measure this invariant.

value.rationale: The scale 3^k is intrinsic to the substitution, not an arbitrary slice. The result settles a natural cyclic invariant at every such scale, quantifies how far it is from the abelian count, and gives a structural criterion identifying exactly the weights with one rather than two necklaces. The marked-gap technique explains the counting law rather than just listing computed values.
residual_risks: No all-length cyclic-complexity formula or full-rotation multiplicity theorem is claimed.
